what: Four color blobs fixed behind the screen move to a different stage per section — when the top edge of a section (data-blob-scene) touches the center line of the screen (the bottom edge when scrolling up), the panel’s data-scene becomes that section’s name, and blob position, size and width slide over 1s cubic-bezier(.5,1,.89,1). enter: if fly, the blobs at first fly in from off-screen (several times the screen width and height away) at 0x scale and opacity .5, settle into place over 3s power1.inOut (each delayed by its data-at seconds), and once all have settled the panel fires fx:entered

options.[data-fx-part=blob]: Chunk (child, with an svg inside) — each stage’s position is set in the consuming CSS via [data-scene="Name"] [data-fx-part=blob]
options.data-from: Chunk child attribute ‹x y› — starting position before flying in (multiples of screen width · height), e.g. 1.2 0
options.data-at: Chunk child property — fly-in start delay (seconds), default index × .5
options.enter: If fly, it flies in at the start — if absent, only the stage changes
options.wait: if true, it does not fly in until fx:enter is fired on the panel (when lifting the loader after all images are loaded)
options.attr: Attribute to read the section name from, default data-blob-scene
options.body: If given, the body also gets that prefix + section name class (original section-*)
options.start · end: Lines where a section switches the stage, default top center · bottom center
options.--fx-dur · --fx-ease: Travel duration and curve (CSS variable), default 1s · cubic-bezier(.5,1,.89,1)

from.where: index.html .kg-bg — blue, red, pink and green blobs fly in after 0·1·.5·1.5s delays from the positions (1.2, 0)·(.8, .8)·(−.8, 1.5)·(−.8, 0), and for each section (concept·campus·visual·movie·anniversary·information) body.section-* changes their position and width. The original sets a 1s transition on the figure while GSAP writes transform, so while the blobs fly in, CSS follows a beat behind and they glide softly — same structure, so the same feel

note: Since transition: all is applied to the chunk figure and GSAP writes transform, the rotate in each stage’s CSS is hidden by the inline transform once the chunk has flown in and no longer changes — the original behaves the same. To change the angle too, apply rotate to the inner svg
